findings.title: Doctor check uses MINIMAL_CONFIG — user step model overrides silently not validated
findings.rationale: The doctor model-existence check uses `MINIMAL_CONFIG = { version: 1, agents: {} }` and `BUILTIN_MODEL_REGISTRY` (not the user's merged registry) to collect effective models from STANDARD_DESCRIPTOR. This means user-configured step model overrides (e.g. `steps.design.model = 'claude-defunct-99'`) are never applied during doctor validation. A user with a stale model in their step config will see `specrunner doctor` report PASS but `specrunner run` throw CONFIG_INVALID — false assurance from the diagnostic tool. The preflight (pipeline-run.ts) correctly uses the actual config and mergeModelRegistry. D7 documents this as a structural constraint (doctor has no request type / reviewer snapshot), but the asymmetry undermines the doctor's purpose of pre-validating configuration.

options.label: Accept as documented structural constraint
options.consequence: Doctor only validates base step hard-coded default models. User step overrides are caught by preflight (run-time) but not doctor. Add explicit documentation that doctor model-existence check does not cover user config overrides.

options.label: Fix by passing actual user config to doctor check
options.consequence: Add rawConfig?: SpecRunnerConfig to DoctorContext and use it in collectEffectiveModels call. This eliminates the false assurance but requires DoctorContext interface change and ensuring rawConfig is properly injected in doctor.ts.

findings.title: Double invocation of 6-level resolution chain creates model/configPath divergence risk
findings.rationale: Lines 82-87 call both `getStepExecutionConfig(config, stepName, stepDefaults, requestType).model` AND `traceStepExecutionConfig(config, stepName, stepDefaults, requestType)` with identical arguments. The model value for validation comes from getStepExecutionConfig; the configPath for error messages comes from traceStepExecutionConfig. Both functions implement the same 6-level resolution chain independently. If either is updated without the other, error messages would show a model+configPath pair where the configPath does not correspond to the actual model that was resolved — producing misleading CONFIG_INVALID messages. The fix is to use only traceStepExecutionConfig and read `traced.fields.model.value` as the model, eliminating the redundant getStepExecutionConfig call.

findings.title: Resume path skips model existence validation — implicit assumption models remain valid across resume
findings.rationale: assertEffectiveModelsExist is only called in PipelineRunCommand.prepare(). ResumeCommand.prepare() has no equivalent call. The implicit assumption is 'a model valid at job start remains valid at resume time.' If a model is deprecated between job start and resume, the pipeline will fail mid-execution (at the SDK call site) instead of at preflight. This creates an asymmetry with assertProviderReadiness, which runs for all CommandRunner.execute() calls (including resume) via the outer guard in runner.ts. This is explicitly within the design scope limitation, but the behavioral difference from assertProviderReadiness may be unexpected.

options.label: Accept as explicit scope limitation
options.consequence: Resume path does not re-validate models. A deprecated model discovered at resume time causes mid-run halt instead of clean preflight CONFIG_INVALID. Document this in design.md as a known gap.

options.label: Add assertEffectiveModelsExist to ResumeCommand.prepare()
options.consequence: Resume path re-validates models. Requires ResumeCommand to have access to the composed descriptor at prepare() time. Adds another SDK session to the resume latency.

observations.title: ANTHROPIC_MODEL_ALIASES and registry aliases co-located but must be kept in sync manually
observations.rationale: ANTHROPIC_MODEL_ALIASES (Set) and the alias entries in BUILTIN_MODEL_REGISTRY are defined in the same file and currently agree. However they are maintained separately — adding an alias to one but not the other would cause a subtle mismatch: registry entry without alias set entry would cause the alias to be validated against supportedModels() (and fail); alias set entry without registry entry would cause resolveProvider to throw CONFIG_INVALID. Current state is correct and co-location mitigates the risk, but there is no compile-time enforcement.

observations.title: STANDARD_DESCRIPTOR import creates new core/doctor → core/pipeline coupling
observations.rationale: Previously src/core/doctor/ had no imports from src/core/pipeline/. The new model-existence check imports STANDARD_DESCRIPTOR directly from pipeline/registry.ts. This is allowed per the DSM (domain-to-domain) and typecheck passes, but it adds a dependency on the entire pipeline definition to the doctor module. If STANDARD_DESCRIPTOR is ever split or the registry refactored, this import will need updating.

observations.title: Lazy-loaded supported-models probe is not cached — new factory per call
observations.rationale: In LocalRuntime.listSupportedModels, the lazy-imported createClaudeSupportedModelsProbe() is not stored back to this.supportedModelsProbe after first use. Each call creates a new probe factory. This is consistent with the assertProviderReadiness pattern and harmless in practice (only called once per run), but differs from injection (where the same probe instance is reused across calls). Not a correctness issue.
